passage:
"Darshan, go on, give Madhav Uncle a kiss. He came all this way," said Mummy.
"Come here, champ, one kiss!" Madhav said, bending down with open arms.
Darshan hid behind Mummy's legs. "No."
"Darshan, be polite," Mummy began, then looked at his face and paused. "Beta, does it feel yucky?"
He nodded.
"Then you do not have to. Would you like to wave or give a high five?"
He held out his palm. Madhav laughed and tapped it lightly. "High five it is!"
"Your body is yours," Mummy whispered.

qa.q: What did Darshan offer Madhav in the end?
How does Darshan feel about giving the kiss?
qa.a: He is uncomfortable: he hides behind Mummy's legs, says no, and nods when she asks if it feels yucky.

qa.q: What did Mummy do that respected Darshan's no?
qa.a: She looked at his face, changed her mind, offered a wave or a high five, and told him his body is his own. 🤍

qa.q: How might Madhav see Darshan's refusal?
qa.a: He seems to take it in good part, since he laughs and accepts the high five; to him the kiss was probably meant as friendly.

grounding: A child is told to kiss a visiting uncle, feels uncomfortable, and the parent changes course and respects the no.

passage:
From Nazia, Rajni's ammi, in our parenting-group notebook.
Tonight Rajni's Chacha visited and said, "Come, give Chacha a big kiss!" I said, "Go on, Rajni, you must." She went stiff and pressed against the door, her eyes on the floor. Then I remembered what we talked about in group. I knelt and said, "You don't have to kiss anyone. Would you like to wave or do a high five?" She chose a high five. Chacha laughed a bit awkwardly, but agreed. At bedtime she said, "My body is mine, Ammi." I said, "Yes. Always."

qa.q: What greeting did Rajni choose instead of a kiss?
What does Rajni going stiff by the door suggest she felt?
qa.a: She felt uncomfortable and pressured, not wanting to kiss Chacha even though she was told she must.

qa.q: What did Nazia change, and why was it right?
qa.a: She took back "you must" and offered a wave or high five, respecting Rajni's no and teaching her that her body belongs to her.

qa.q: How might Chacha feel when Rajni gives a high five?
qa.a: He may feel a little awkward at first but can still enjoy a warm greeting that Rajni chose.

grounding: A young girl is told to kiss a visiting uncle, feels uncomfortable, and her mother changes course and respects her no.

passage: Chinmay Mama had come from the town with a bag of guavas. "Lakshmi! Give Mama a kiss!" Lakshmi looked at her feet and twisted her frock. "Go on," Amma said. "Don't be rude. You must." Lakshmi's face went red. She shook her head a tiny bit. Appa put down his cup. "She doesn't have to kiss if she doesn't want to. Lakshmi, want to give Mama a high five, or wave?" Lakshmi's shoulders dropped. She gave Chinmay Mama a big, loud high five. Mama laughed. Later Appa told Amma quietly, "Her body is hers to decide." Amma nodded slowly.

qa.q: What did Chinmay Mama bring from the town?
qa.a: He brought a bag of guavas.

qa.q: How was Lakshmi feeling when she twisted her frock?
qa.a: She felt uncomfortable and embarrassed, pressured to kiss her uncle when she didn't want to.

qa.q: What did Appa do that a wise parent would do?
qa.a: He respected Lakshmi's no and offered her a wave or high five, then explained to Amma that her body is hers to decide.

qa.q: Why might Amma first insist on the kiss?
qa.a: She may worry that saying no to a relative is rude and want Lakshmi to show respect, until Appa helps her see it differently.

grounding: A young girl is told she must kiss a visiting uncle, feels uncomfortable, and her father respects her no and offers a high five.
